This battle was a significant military victory for Conall and his forces, and it helped to establish his position as a major power in the region. The battle also marked a turning point in the political history of Scotland, as it led to the decline of the power of the High King of Dál Riata and the rise of the kingdoms of Strathclyde and Northumbria.

Conall's legacy can be seen in the many place names and cultural artifacts that still exist today, which reflect the significant cultural exchange and influence that occurred between Scotland and Ireland during this period.
